approach.method_basis: The Parent starts from the best supplied molecule and walks through local graph edits. Its neighborhood includes direct exchanges of an aromatic nitrogen with a carbon in the same six-member ring, preserving composition. It normalizes molecular identities, rejects duplicates and uses short-lived inverse local-motif restrictions to admit the first full batch of neighbors. After real feedback it moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor, even when every neighbor is worse, and keeps a separate best archive. Equal batch maxima are currently resolved by canonical text order; memory then receives the selected transition's actual changes.
approach.novelty: Add a minimum-heavy-atom tie rule: among exact accepted batch maxima, choose the molecule with the fewest heavy atoms and use canonical order for any remaining tie. This makes measured score equality an opportunity to avoid unnecessary growth before the next neighborhood is generated. Earlier siblings changed the edit menu, chemical admissibility or inverse memory. The branch-deletion experiment established access to compact proposals but weak retention and later regrowth; this experiment changes only the choice among existing equally best accepted neighbors. No sibling in the supplied history has tested this size preference at feedback.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-abcd951ab7cc retains the repaired inverse-motif walk and aromatic nitrogen relocation, with complete three-replica macro mean 0.5217591163770486 and population deviation 0.006329100643035156. Its next-state rule gives canonical text order the final say among equal accepted batch maxima, which can select graph growth without any measured score advantage. A read-only scan of all fifteen Parent task logs reconstructs 435 nonempty accepted transitions and reproduces every lexical winner. Exactly 26 batches have multiple exact accepted maxima, containing 64 maximizing candidates; seven tie sets contain unequal heavy-atom counts. In three batches the lexical winner has one more heavy atom than another accepted maximum. All three choices are source-score plateaus and choose add_path products; two occur in deco_hop replica 0 and one in deco_hop replica 2. These are same-batch scored alternatives, not an inferred alternative trajectory. The passive minimum-size comparison leaves the other 432 winners unchanged. Related sibling n-0e56e71777c4 made 69 compact whole-branch prunings available, but only four won their batch, all later regrew, typical emitted size stayed essentially unchanged, and every replica regressed. That finding motivates examining how existing equally scored alternatives become current states; it does not establish that smaller molecules always improve score. The complete Parent comparison is retained in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0012-00-improve-L16.plan-audit.json.
hypothesis: Among exact accepted-score batch maxima, select the candidate with the fewest heavy atoms before applying the inherited canonical lexical fallback, so an equally scored larger neighbor cannot become current solely because of its canonical spelling.

finding_summary.headline: Six smaller tied winners were executed, but later scores did not improve
finding_summary.insights: Canonical ordering did sometimes choose unnecessary growth at an exactly tied score, so this experiment establishes a real selection opportunity. Avoiding that growth did not preserve a permanently compact or more productive walk: every changed choice was followed by a later growth move, and the six-transition plateau containing the first seed-2 change kept its original length. Mean proposal size in the affected task decreased by only 0.30 heavy atoms, with the median unchanged at 38. Smaller also did not mean chemically simpler: one changed choice introduced a carbon-sulfur triple bond, and the molecular assessment still finds reactive heteroatom attachments and questionable complete structures. Half of the changed choices altered bonds or elements without shrinking their own source; the other half deleted one atom. The poorer later results therefore concern changed chemical neighborhoods and memory provenance, not an isolated effect of size. In the seed-2 continuation, accepted source-beating neighbors fell from 19 to nine. The evidence narrows the opportunity to sparse exact ties in one objective family and makes chemically meaningful tie preferences or persistence of compact states worth testing separately; neither has a demonstrated score benefit here.
finding_summary.results: The rule changed six of 435 accepted transitions, all on equal-score plateaus in deco_hop seeds 0 and 2. Each selected an already scored maximum with one or two fewer heavy atoms than the lexical alternative, saving 10 atoms across those same-batch comparisons. All selected identities reached the actual current state and memory update. The other 429 choices, the immediate maximum score, canonical fallback and independent archive rule passed reconstruction checks. The three-seed panel mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.520655: paired change -0.001104 against the preregistered +0.002 minimum. Deco_hop endpoints fell by 0.001632 in seed 0 and 0.014925 in seed 2; every other task/replica scored trajectory was identical. The local tie mechanism is confirmed, while its expected score benefit was not observed.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich, often sulfur-heavy molecules retain recognizable motifs but lack reliable chemical plausibility and specified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: All five supplied tasks are covered; none lacks trajectories. Each has 900 recorded molecules across three seeds, including 870 optimizer proposals. These are branched, polycyclic organic graphs with substantial aromatic content, ordinary carbonyl and amine groups, and frequent sulfur and halogen substitution. Every task has string-level ring_closure_rate 1.0; aromatic_atom_rate, meaning presence of aromatic SMILES atoms rather than their atom fraction, ranges from 0.7184 to 1.0. There is no shortage of rings. Passive RDKit inspection of the supplied trajectories gives task median heavy-atom counts of 25, 38, 36, 35 and 29 in the fixed task order. All optimizer proposals parse in the matching environment. Parsing establishes graph acceptance, not stability, a synthesis route or a realizable conformation. Many later structures combine multiple bonds to sulfur, heteroatom-halogen attachments, difficult ring bridges and unspecified stereogenic centers. All five digest charged_rate and stereocentre_rate values are 0.0. This means no explicit charge or tetrahedral stereochemical notation; it does not mean the molecules cannot ionize or are achiral. Structural diversity is moderate: the observed families differ across tasks and seeds, but many distinct graphs remain decorated or distorted descendants of recognizable starting scaffolds. Relative to Parent n-abcd951ab7cc, molecule identities and recorded scores are identical throughout every seed of zaleplon_mpo, drd2_docking, median_2 and sitagliptin_mpo, and throughout deco_hop seed 1. The changed deco_hop trajectories retain the same broad imide/heteroaromatic chemistry; smaller average atom count does not establish improved chemical quality. The digest final_molecules excerpts cover only seed 2 evaluations 295-300 and are final proposals, not the best archive or a summary of every seed. All numerical graph descriptions below were passively derived from the provided SMILES; synthetic plausibility and missing chemistry are qualitative readings. Absent features have no measured counterfactual score, so an unseen objective-specific pharmacophore cannot be inferred from these records.

per_task.generated_character: Proposals contain 21-29 heavy atoms, median 25, with median three perceived rings. The best seed-2 molecule at evaluation 133 is a substituted benzofuran anilide: an aromatic fused oxygen heterocycle, an N-chlorinated carboxamide, an aminophenyl group, a thiol and a carbon bearing amine and chlorine. The seed-1 high scorer at evaluation 61 is a more recognizable ethoxy/methyl/thiol-substituted indole carboxanilide; the seed-0 high scorer at evaluation 81 is a benzothiophene aryl ketone with aminomethoxy and chloromethyl substituents. Later proposals also contain bridged, partly dearomatized oxygen/sulfur frameworks. The ring and aromatic presence rates are 1.0 and 0.9563; halogen presence is 0.7552. The indole anilide looks appreciably more synthetically approachable than the N-haloamide and later bridged sulfur structures. Chemistry and scores match the Parent trajectories.
liabilities: The best example contains an N-chloroamide and a carbon bearing both amine and chlorine, while other cited examples contain N-F/N-O bonds or thiols; these raise stability and handling questions.
The final framework contains unusual sulfur multiple bonding and an N-N substituent. Complex ring connectivity and unspecified configuration reduce confidence in a straightforward synthesis.
missing_features: Reliable retention of the compact fused heteroaromatic carbonyl architecture: many lower-scoring neighbors expand or dearomatize the core, or replace the carbonyl linkage.

A broad set of ordinary substituent variants around that observed high-scoring architecture without accompanying N-halogenation, labile sulfur features or elaborate bridges; such variants are not established by the top excerpt.
Specified configurations for the stereogenic substituted carbons and bridged products; the records do not establish that adding stereochemical specification would improve this score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145; related compact fused heteroaromatic carbonyl compounds reach 0.39905049777278273 and 0.41003927643747895. The benzothiophene ketone scores 0.393567030299894, so an amide is not obligatory within the observed high-scoring family. Low optimizer examples at 0.021532846118034143 and 0.023463222457063 have expanded/dearomatized cores despite retaining an aryl carbonyl; the evaluation-42 example that replaces the carbonyl linkage with a substituted saturated carbon scores 0.03343008011310944. The association supports compact fused heteroaromatic/carbonyl architecture more than indiscriminate ring editing. It does not isolate a causal benefit for thiols or N-halogenation. The final seed-2 sulfur-bridged hydrazine-containing proposal scores 0.3852230774700024, showing that a fairly high score can coexist with less conventional chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: These are the largest and most flexible proposal families: 30-49 heavy atoms, median 38, median four perceived rings and nine rotatable bonds. The high-scoring seed-0 family retains a fused nitrogen heteroaromatic imide/thioimide-like core and a densely substituted aniline-derived ring while extending imine, ether and ester-containing side chains. Its best excerpt contains 46-heavy-atom molecules with bromine, chlorine and fluorine, sulfur-chlorine bonds and carbon-sulfur triple bonds; one has sulfur between two triple bonds. Final seed-2 proposals instead carry heteroaromatic fused rings, a conjugated polyene ether side chain, carbonyls and N-bromination; one final example includes a hydroperoxide. Ring and aromatic presence rates are both 1.0, halogen presence 0.7655. Ordinary heteroaromatic cores remain recognizable, but the decorated products have questionable synthetic plausibility. Across all proposals the Child mean heavy-atom count is 38.60344827586207 versus Parent 38.90344827586207; the median stays 38. Passive graph counts find sulfur triple bonds in 110 of 870 Child proposals versus 1 of 870 Parent proposals, and N/O/S-halogen bonds in 442 versus 277. Thus the modest size difference accompanies a different, still problematic set of functional groups.
liabilities: Carbon-sulfur triple bonds and sulfur between two triple bonds are extraordinary medicinal-chemistry linkages. Their acceptance as molecular graphs gives no synthesis or stability evidence.
S-Cl, N-Br, imine-rich side chains and a cited hydroperoxide create reactivity concerns independently of heavy-atom count.
Long flexible side chains, crowded substitution and unspecified stereogenic centers complicate a credible synthesis and a defined molecular product.
missing_features: Chemically ordinary, compact realizations of the retained heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangement with varied substituent placement: the best observed family remains large and densely decorated.

Systematic replacement of unusual side-chain bonds by conventional linkages while retaining the scored core. An ordinary alkyne already shares the maximum, so the displayed sulfur triple bonds are not shown to be required.
Stable and stereochemically specified versions of the branched late-stage structures; their score benefit is unmeasured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aromatic imide scores 0.548381482770623. Early disrupted-core proposals score 0.526081691583997 and 0.5286081645773063, whereas the heavily decorated seed-0 family reaches 0.6145389662714401. Several chemically distinct side-chain bond patterns, including sulfur-containing and ordinary carbon-carbon triple bonds, share that exact recorded maximum. The gradient therefore associates retained heteroaromatic/carbonyl organization and expanded substitution with higher scores, but does not identify exotic sulfur bonding as necessary. Final seed-2 examples span 0.5518599963349826 to 0.5942930760374979 while retaining reactive motifs. The recorded best endpoints for changed seeds 0 and 2 are 0.6145389662714401 and 0.5942930760374979, compared with Parent 0.6161710037174721 and 0.6092182584436399; seed 1 remains 0.605139548855754. These are paired observations of different trajectories, not evidence that an individual sulfur bond or size change caused the endpoint difference.

per_task.generated_character: Proposals contain 32-43 heavy atoms, median 36, with median four perceived rings and two aromatic rings. High-scoring structures combine phenolic and halogenated aryl groups with aliphatic nitrogen centers, aminomethyl or amino substituents and sulfur-containing rings or linkers. The best seed-2 proposal at evaluation 291 has 32 heavy atoms, two benzene rings, a primary aminomethyl group and additional substituted ring nitrogens, embedded in an unusual sulfur-rich polycycle. The seed-0 high scorer includes an aziridine, an amino-substituted nitrogen ring and a sulfur-sulfur multiple-bonded terminus; another seed produces a heavily bridged sulfur/nitrogen framework. These molecules do contain basic-amine candidates; describing a universal absence of amines would be wrong. Ring and aromatic presence rates are 1.0, and halogen presence is 0.9966. RDKit flags unassigned potential tetrahedral centers in every optimizer proposal, while the digest stereocentre and charged rates are zero. Chemistry and scores match the Parent trajectories.
liabilities: The best molecule contains sulfur-sulfur multiple bonding and unusual multiple bonds to sulfur within rings; another high scorer contains a cumulated nitrogen/carbon/sulfur linkage.
The aziridine-bearing high scorer introduces a strained nitrogen ring alongside reactive sulfur chemistry. Other bridged structures have unresolved stereochemical and conformational feasibility.
High halogen prevalence and retained aromatic groups are clear compositional features, but no solubility, exposure or synthetic-route data were provided.
missing_features: A demonstrated high-scoring realization of the observed aryl/amine arrangement using ordinary, readily interpretable heterocycles and linkers instead of the unusual sulfur frameworks in the top excerpt.

Defined stereochemistry and explicit ionization-state coverage for the available amine centers. Neutral SMILES do not imply nonbasic molecules, and these records do not measure whether alternate protonation states help.
Clean local comparisons that preserve the aryl/amine arrangement while simplifying ring connectivity; the observed gradient otherwise mixes changes in functional groups, rings and composition.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial biaryl carboxylic acid/carboxamide/N-sulfonyl nitrogen-ring structure scores 0.01904115112334333; its close low optimizer variants score 0.007468397818197266 and 0.009665119877745591. Later less oxygenated aryl/amine-rich sulfur frameworks reach 0.8856242185485628 and 0.9148143511682032. The observed gradient is consistent with reorganizing acid/amide/sulfonamide-rich chemistry into aryl-linked aliphatic amines, but many structural changes occur together. Sulfur/carbon substitutions among cited seed-2 examples tie exactly at 0.8825461379136246, so those atom identities are not individually resolved by these measurements. Late structures remain sensitive to connectivity: the seed-2 final excerpt ranges from 0.04252669549740123 to 0.8474359962807467. No binding pose, protonation dependence or experimentally viable pharmacophore is established by the recorded scores.

per_task.generated_character: Proposals contain 27-45 heavy atoms, median 35, with median four perceived rings and two aromatic rings. The best seed-0 family is a densely bridged pyridine/phenyl framework with alkyl substitution, a tertiary lactam and an N-O bridge. The top example has 31 heavy atoms; its ring perception includes medium and larger cycles rather than a simple collection of independent fused rings. Other seeds develop brominated aryl/sulfur/hydrazine structures or larger sulfur-containing bridged lactams with alcohol and ether substituents. RDKit finds at least one perceived ring of size eight or greater in 677 of 870 proposals, which describes graph topology rather than proving strain. Ring and aromatic presence rates are 1.0; halogen presence is lower than the other tasks at 0.3529. The amide and aromatic pieces are familiar, but elaborate bridges and reactive attachments make many complete structures difficult synthetic propositions. Chemistry and scores match the Parent trajectories.
liabilities: The top family requires an elaborate bridged ring assembly with an N-O connection and unspecified stereogenic centers; recognizable fragments do not by themselves make the complete synthesis straightforward.

The low brominated example contains an aryl O-Br bond, brominated side chains and N-N substitution. A final example similarly contains an O-Cl attachment, and final sulfur frameworks retain unusual sulfur valence.
missing_features: A well-sampled family of simpler, chemically conventional ring frameworks retaining the observed aromatic/lactam organization; upper-scoring examples cluster around a difficult bridged framework.
Defined configurations and demonstrably realizable geometry for the bridged structures; the SMILES specify connectivity without resolving the possible stereoisomers.
Conservative functional-group alternatives that preserve the observed arrangement while removing N-O, O-halogen and unusual sulfur attachments; no score benefit for those replacements is established.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aromatic imide scores 0.1678386594791329. Its ring-opened carbonyl/urea-containing relative scores 0.1263981386214515; a related extended side-chain example scores 0.12467972074136988. The bridged pyridine/phenyl/lactam family reaches 0.21196904390980506, with several alkyl and ring-size variants close to that value. This associates an organized ring-linked aromatic/lactam arrangement with the upper observed scores, rather than simply adding atoms or polar functionality. A bulky brominated/hydrazine/sulfur example scores 0.12870267321446027. The final seed-2 bridged sulfur lactams reach 0.18814867381840605 and end at 0.18220097615153677, below the best seed-0 family. These records do not establish that additional bridges, the N-O bond or sulfur chemistry are necessary for the objective.

per_task.generated_character: These proposals are compact by atom count but unusually dense in rings and sulfur: 25-33 heavy atoms, median 29, median six perceived rings and only two rotatable bonds. The best seed-1 molecule has 30 heavy atoms including five sulfur atoms and three fluorines, a carbonyl-bearing nitrogen heterocycle, a hydroxyl-bearing thioether substituent and a multiply bridged unsaturated cage. The high seed-0 example has 30 heavy atoms but eight sulfur atoms and no perceived aromatic atoms. Final seed-2 examples are nonaromatic sulfur-rich cages carrying carbonyl/aldehyde and N-fluoro amidine-like functionality. Ring presence is 1.0, aromatic presence 0.7184 and halogen presence 0.7; aromaticity is therefore common but is not universal or dominant in every high-scoring structure. RDKit finds a three- or four-membered perceived ring in 712 of 870 proposals, and unassigned potential tetrahedral centers in 816. Small-ring presence alone is not a defect, but these crowded, multiply connected sulfur frameworks have particularly doubtful synthetic and geometric plausibility. Chemistry and scores match the Parent trajectories.
liabilities: Multiple bonds to sulfur, sulfur-sulfur connectivity and heavily bridged small-ring topology are repeated in the best molecules; a low heavy-atom count does not remove these liabilities.
The seed-0 high scorer contains an acyl fluoride, while final examples contain N-F and a carbonyl-linked S-Cl group. These functional groups create reactivity concerns beyond the global score.
Unspecified stereogenic centers and dense unsaturation within bridged frameworks leave chemical identity and conformational feasibility unresolved.
missing_features: Chemically ordinary structures that separate compactness, fluorination and carbonyl placement from the unusual sulfur cage chemistry; these properties are entangled in the high-scoring excerpt.
Stereochemically specified and geometrically credible versions of the polycyclic products. The best seed-1 graph has seven RDKit-flagged unassigned potential tetrahedral centers.

Independent exploration of conventional heterocycles and carbonyl-bearing linkers at similar molecular size, sufficient to learn which observed features matter without assuming that cage density is required.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aromatic imide scores 0.0020944534688323298; an expanded carbonyl-containing neighbor scores 7.590554525032884e-10. Later compact fluorinated sulfur cages reach 0.5903526424693334, 0.55705130532462 and 0.5527071687189122. However, an already sulfur-rich, ring-dense intermediate scores only 1.0546805269255595e-09. Sulfur loading or cage formation alone therefore does not explain the gradient. In the final seed-2 excerpt the cage bearing a carbonyl-linked S-Cl group scores 0.004199910554494925, whereas the smaller aldehyde-containing cage at evaluation 297 scores 0.4484554129767839. The association suggests sensitivity to detailed composition, carbonyl identity and ring connectivity within this compact family, not a monotone preference for more rings, sulfur or aromatic atoms. Nothing shown identifies a missing target-specific amine, fluorination pattern or stereoisomer as the objective solution.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited high-scoring molecules include carbon-sulfur triple bonds, sulfur between two triple bonds, sulfur-sulfur multiple bonding and N-halogen or S-halogen attachments. In the changed trajectory family, sulfur-triple-bond proposals increase from 1 of 870 in the Parent to 110 of 870 in the Child, while mean heavy-atom count decreases only from 38.90344827586207 to 38.60344827586207. An ordinary carbon-carbon alkyne in the digest shares the same recorded score as several exotic sulfur variants.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably distinguish ordinary sulfur and heteroatom functional groups from graph-valid but chemically exceptional linkages.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically interpretable alternatives within conventional sulfur oxidation states and functional-group classes, and track reactive heteroatom attachments separately from graph validity. Apply that capability uniformly to any supplied molecule; assess its consequences with observed feedback rather than assuming that removing sulfur or all heteroatom-heteroatom bonds is beneficial.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited upper-scoring families include compact fused heteroaromatic carbonyl compounds and organized aromatic/lactam frameworks. Their lower-scoring examples include core dearomatization, ring expansion, ring opening and replacement of a carbonyl linkage by substituted saturated carbon. Other high-scoring examples tolerate such changes, so this is a missing controlled chemical comparison, not a universal rule that aromaticity or a particular carbonyl must be frozen.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve recognizable aromatic and carbonyl architecture while varying the surrounding chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expose coherent local substitutions and conventional alternative ring frameworks that retain a recognizable functional-group arrangement. Make it possible to compare changes in attachment position or peripheral groups without simultaneously changing core valence, ring topology and carbonyl identity, using the same chemical rules for every request.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All five digest stereocentre_rate values are 0.0. Passive RDKit inspection finds unassigned potential tetrahedral centers in 547, 459, 870, 740 and 816 of the 870 proposals in each respective digest task. The cited compact sulfur cage at the highest score within its family has seven such centers; even the more conventional-looking substituted benzofuran has an unspecified center.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has no displayed coverage of explicitly specified stereochemistry despite repeatedly producing stereogenic and bridged structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support chemically defined stereoisomeric representations of generated graphs and preserve their configurations through identity handling. Treat bridged-ring geometry as a separate feasibility question from SMILES validity. This addresses a missing chemical dimension; the supplied scores do not establish that stereochemical enumeration itself yields a gain.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The changed proposal family has a slightly lower mean heavy-atom count than its Parent but more heteroatom-halogen attachments: 442 versus 277 of 870 proposals. Elsewhere the digest contains 30-heavy-atom high-scoring cages with five or eight sulfur atoms, and a 31-heavy-atom high scorer with elaborate bridged aromatic/lactam connectivity. Atom count therefore misses both reactive functional groups and difficult ring assembly.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator can make smaller molecular graphs without producing chemically simpler or more readily synthesizable molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expose simplifications that preserve meaningful functional groups while reducing unnecessary ring bridges or reactive attachments, and describe those effects independently of atom count. A compactness preference needs chemically conventional alternative graphs to choose among; smaller size alone is not evidence of improved stability, synthesis or three-dimensional feasibility.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest charged_rate is 0.0. The cited aryl/amine-rich high-scoring structures contain primary aminomethyl groups and substituted aliphatic nitrogens; the starting and lower-scoring set includes carboxylic acids. Thus ionizable functionality is present, but formal-charge alternatives are not shown. Neutral notation alone does not establish the state of these molecules under any assay condition.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not explore explicit ionization states even where it already contains potentially basic amines and acidic functional groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically justified protonation-state alternatives for existing ionizable groups, with consistent identity representation and no inference of hidden task identity or assay conditions. The missing capability is state coverage, not universal addition of a basic ring or a charge; any benefit would require the ordinary supplied feedback.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
